purpose: Revision02 read-only preflight; no sensitive material or generated values persisted
proof: The unchanged driver issues a separate native character message for each character of the sensitive input.
The fixed private-world listener emits the complete current sensitive value at each input event.
Under the requested repair the first nonempty length-one buffer must immediately join the session's permanent known set.
Static comparison, without logging that buffer, confirms that both immutable required literal page text leaves contain it.
Whole-leaf redaction removes the literal demanded by each assertion; a typed publication block produces no successful observation for those assertions.
A green closure therefore requires human reconciliation; filtering or forgetting that short buffer would violate the new security requirement.

currentProductDefect.inspection: Input replaces pending state on trusted prefix growth without immediately adding each observed value to the permanent set.

openDecision.securityRequirement: Every observed nonempty sensitive buffer, including length-one buffers, remains known; a matching short value requires whole-leaf redaction or typed publication denial, never a minimum-length exception.
openDecision.immutableTestRequirement: Two historical native tests require publication of literal page text that contains the first length-one buffer produced by their unchanged character-by-character UI driver.
openDecision.scope: Static compatibility proof about the authorized repair and immutable assertions, not a native execution or a new engine-enforcement limit.
openDecision.consequence: Correct short-buffer protection cannot simultaneously preserve those required literal page-derived leaves. Typed publication denial also prevents the required successful BrowserObservation assertions.
openDecision.requestedDirection: Human reconciliation of the affected test-observability contract, preserving the non-exposure invariant and historical evidence. No test/driver/fixture/assertion change is authorized or performed here.
